prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place named in the Gospel of Matthew
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land, city or region named in the Gospel of Matthew
prompts.note: Bethlehem and Jericho are in the West Bank (PSE); players may pin ISR, which is also correct for Jerusalem and Galilee.
prompts.summary: Matthew ranges well beyond Galilee. The infant Jesus was carried from Bethlehem to Egypt, his fame spread through Syria and Decapolis, and he went to the coasts of Tyre and Sidon and beyond the Jordan. Jesus cited the men of Nineveh, and Simon of Cyrene, from today's Libya, carried his cross.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jerusalem, Nazareth and Galilee run through the whole Gospel (Matthew 2:1, 22-23).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph took the young child and Mary into Egypt until Herod died (Matthew 2:14-15).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea and passed through Jericho (Matthew 2:1; 20:29).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Jesus departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 15:21).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: His fame went throughout all Syria, and crowds came from Decapolis (Matthew 4:24-25).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Jesus named the men of Nineveh, and the genealogy names the carrying away to Babylon (Matthew 12:41; 1:11).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Jesus came into the coasts of Judea beyond Jordan, east of the river (Matthew 19:1).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: Simon, who carried the cross, was a man of Cyrene, in eastern Libya (Matthew 27:32).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that was home to a wife of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses or Boaz
prompts.text_original: A present-day country that was the homeland of a wife of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses or Boaz: Sarai from Ur, Hagar the Egyptian, Rebekah, Leah and Rachel from Laban's family at Haran, Asenath of On, Zipporah of Midian, Moses' wife from Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt, and Ruth the Moabitess
prompts.note: Bible Ethiopia (Cush) lay mostly in today's Sudan, reaching into southern Egypt; modern Ethiopia is not counted.
prompts.summary: Many founding wives of Israel came from abroad. Sarai left Ur with Abram, Hagar was Egyptian, and Rebekah, Leah and Rachel came from Laban's family at Haran. Joseph married Asenath of On in Egypt, Moses married Zipporah of Midian and an Ethiopian woman, and Ruth the Moabitess became great-grandmother of David.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Hagar, Abraham's handmaid and wife, was an Egyptian; Joseph married Asenath, daughter of the priest of On (Gen 16:1-3; 41:45).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Sarai went out with Abram from Ur of the Chaldees (Gen 11:29-31); BD Ur identifies it with Mugheir near the Persian Gulf.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Boaz married Ruth the Moabitess (Ruth 1:4; 4:10, 13).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Rebekah, Leah and Rachel came from the household of Laban, who lived at Haran (Gen 24:29; 27:43; 29:4-6); Church Bible Map 9 says Rebekah, Rachel, Leah, Bilhah and Zilpah came from the Haran area.

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Moses dwelt in the land of Midian and married Zipporah, daughter of its priest (Ex 2:15-21); Church Bible Map 9 plots Midian east of the Gulf of Aqaba.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married (Num 12:1); Bible Ethiopia was the Nile land south of Egypt.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Portuguese is an official language and the Church has more than 5,000 members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: A country where Portuguese is an official language and the Church had more than 5,000 members at the end of 2025 (latest figures as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (membership, 31 Dec 2025); Wikipedia country infoboxes (official languages)
prompts.summary: Portuguese is official in nine countries. Five of them had more than 5,000 Latter-day Saints at the end of 2025: Brazil (over 1.5 million), Portugal, Mozambique, Cape Verde and Angola. Guinea-Bissau, Sao Tome and Principe, Equatorial Guinea and Timor-Leste have no published Church membership of that size.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: 1,573,360 members, the largest Portuguese-speaking membership.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: 50,341 members.

answers.name: Cape Verde
answers.fact: 16,334 members, four stakes (latest published figure).

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: 39,282 members, ten stakes.

answers.name: Angola
answers.fact: 8,779 members, two stakes.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where the Book of Mormon has been published, whole or in part, in three or more of its languages.
prompts.text_original: Some countries have had the Book of Mormon published, whole or in part, in three or more languages spoken within their borders. Pin such a country, as recorded in the Church's country chronologies.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Philippines, South Africa, Nigeria, India, Micronesia, Guatemala, Bolivia, DR Congo, Switzerland, Belgium, Hawaii, Mexico
prompts.summary: The Book of Mormon has reached several countries in three or more of their own languages. The Philippines has Tagalog, Cebuano, Pangasinan and Hiligaynon; South Africa has Afrikaans, Zulu, Xhosa and Tswana; Micronesia has Chuukese, Pohnpeian, Yapese and Kosraean. Switzerland and Belgium were covered by the French, German, Italian and Dutch editions of the 1800s.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: English (1830), Hawaiian (1855) and Spanish (1886) editions, among others.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Tagalog, Cebuano and Pangasinan (1998), Hiligaynon (2005), plus Waray and Bikolano selections.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: French, German and Italian editions all appeared in 1852.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Efik selections (1984), Igbo (2000) and Yoruba (2007), plus English.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Afrikaans (1972), Zulu (2003), Xhosa (2000) and Tswana (2003), plus English.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: French and German (1852) and Dutch (1890).

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: Spanish (1886), Quechua selections (1981) and Aymara (1986).

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: French (1852), Lingala (selections 1988, full 2004) and Swahili (2000).

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Spanish (1886), Kaqchikel (1978), Mam (1982-83) and K'ekchi (1983).

answers.name: India
answers.fact: Hindi (1982) plus selections in Telugu, Tamil (1982) and Bengali (1985).

answers.name: Micronesia
answers.fact: Chuukese and Pohnpeian selections (1987), Yapese (2004), Kosraean and Chuukese (2015).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose first temple was dedicated between 1950 and 1980.
prompts.text_original: A country whose first temple was dedicated between 1950 and 1980.
prompts.summary: Between 1950 and 1980 the Church took temples to five new countries: Switzerland (1955), the United Kingdom and New Zealand (1958), Brazil (1978) and Japan (1980). The United States and Canada already had temples; the next wave of first temples began in 1983.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Bern Switzerland Temple, 1955.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London England Temple, 1958.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: São Paulo Brazil Temple, 1978.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Hamilton New Zealand Temple, 1958.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Tokyo Japan Temple, October 1980.
